questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was doing clinical rotation at Haukeland sjykehus, where I went to the orthopedic department and the emergency room. When choosing destination it was important to me that I would be able to communicate with the patients so that I would get the most learning out of my experience at the hospital. Therefore I chose Norway as my destination. I love nature and Bergen is a city surrounded by mountains where nature is no more than 30 minutes away by foot. This too, was a crucial aspect choosing the study destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I loved Bergen! I would definitely do it again and I'm definitely going back to visit soon! The nature at Vestlandet is amazing and I enjoyed many weekend trips on foot, skis and climbing.
At the hospital I loved my time at the orthopedic department, but it would have been nice with a schedule. at the orthopedic department I had a very nice tutor who showed med around the first day and told me where to go each day. I didn't get a schedule at the ER either, which made it hard to know where I should be and when I should be there. On the other hand I got to see many very interesting cases and a lot of different cases. The docters all in all were super nice, both at the ER and the Orthopedic department, but I wouldn't recommend choosing the ER as a part of a clinical rotation. Sometimes it was so hectic it was hard to know what I was supposed to do, and where I was supposed to be. So if I went again I wouldn't choose the ER and I would definitely be more insisting on getting a schedule (on paper) for my time at each department.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I lived in the city center in a sammen flat shared with 3 others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
it's very nice to live in the city. The sammen flats in the city are not very social. If you want to live more social choose Alrek or Fantoft (both further away from the city) or find a place through
Hybel.no
.

questions.answer: The docters were very nice, but they didn't really know what level I was at, so I didn't get to do as much as I would've if I were in Denmark.

questions.answer: clinical rotation is pretty much the same I think, but I'm used to having a schedule for my practice.

questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: clinical rotation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend the orthopedic department. Very sweet doctors who were very aware of you being there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the level at the "BSI friluft" was too high for my personal ski-level, which was kind of sad because they just had ski-trips in the spring.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many activities were available, but they were hard to find. There's not a lot of social activities at the faculty of medicine, there's BLOT and then there are exam parties, that's it. There are a lot of medicine groups though, and I would recommend joining one just to meet some Norwegian students. examples of groups are Klima=Helse and MedHum.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go Tuesday climbing with BSI friluft, it's fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on the city-mountains. Sammen has a student cabin at kvamskogen from where you can go crosscountry skiing I can definitely recommend renting the cabin.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: the culture is very similar to the danish culture, but norwegians are a bit more reserved than Danes I think.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join a group at the faculty, if you get a Norwegian one on one they open up quickly. If you're invited to a party, just go (norwegians are very friendly when drunk).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: that norwegians are a bit more reserved than danes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it's common to just go on a sunday hike or if the weather is good you're expected to be out in nature. And when you're on a fjell, you must say hi.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring hiking boots, skis and raincoat+boots. Enjoy nature it's amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything is expensive, don't worry about money when you're in Norway, just go explore!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: being surrounded by nature and having people around who wanted to explore nature with me. It was amazing to be able to go on trips every weekend.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: in the beginning it was hard to get to know norwegians because I didn't attend any classes, but one and a half months in, the norwegian students started their clinical rotation so I got to meet some people.

questions.answer: Yes
